headline: Semiconductors Ride Solo as Broader Market Retreats into the Weekend
body_html:
Friday's session closed on a decidedly split note, with the semiconductor complex muscling ahead even as six of eight sectors finished in the red. Of 545 names tracked, 339 ended lower against just 205 advances — a lopsided tape that underscored how narrow the day's leadership truly was. Semiconductors gained 2.47%, the only sector to post a meaningful advance, while Homebuilders bore the sharpest pain at –1.62%, followed by Materials at –1.05% and Software at –1.03%.

Memory and equipment names led the charge within semis. Sandisk surged nearly 11%, MaxLinear added 8.17%, and optical-networking specialist Coherent climbed 7.22%. Equipment makers Lam Research and Applied Materials rose 6.98% and 6.51%, respectively, while Seagate Technology rounded out the top gainers with a 6.93% advance. On the other side of the ledger, steelmaker Nucor shed 6.32%, warehouse-automation firm Symbotic fell 6.1%, and Qualcomm dropped 5.82%.

Heading into the new week, geopolitical risk moves to the fore. Houthi forces claimed responsibility for strikes near Riyadh — with flames reported close to the Saudi capital's airport — rattling Gulf equity markets and lifting Middle East tension premiums. World leaders convene at the United Nations amid active conflicts in both the Middle East and Ukraine, while a Meta-linked data-centre bond drew outsized junk-market demand, signalling that infrastructure appetite remains intact despite the broader risk-off mood.

briefs.headline: Houthi Strikes Near Riyadh Rattle Gulf Markets
briefs.body: Houthi forces claimed responsibility for attacks on the Saudi capital, with eyewitnesses reporting flames and black smoke visible near Riyadh's airport. Saudi and broader Gulf equity markets fell in response, adding a fresh geopolitical premium to energy-linked assets and regional risk sentiment heading into the trading week.

briefs.headline: UN General Assembly Opens Against Backdrop of Two Active Wars
briefs.body: World leaders gathered at the United Nations this weekend with the conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East dominating the agenda. Diplomatic signals emerging from the assembly — including Turkey's offer to help meet Saudi military needs under a bilateral defence pact — could shape safe-haven flows and defence-sector positioning through the week.

briefs.headline: Infrastructure Bond Demand Signals Durable Appetite for Data-Centre Build-Out
briefs.body: A junk-rated bond tied to a Meta-affiliated data centre drew blowback demand in its market debut, suggesting credit investors remain willing to fund large-scale computing infrastructure even as equity markets turned cautious. The deal's reception will be watched as a barometer for continued private-capital commitment to AI-related physical infrastructure.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Equipment Names Post Strongest Friday Gains
briefs.body: Lam Research and Applied Materials each rose nearly 7% on Friday, extending a run that has made semi-equipment one of the market's best-performing pockets. The moves tracked broader optimism in memory and storage hardware, raising the question of whether the group can sustain momentum absent a fresh catalyst in the week ahead.

briefs.headline: Steel and Metals Coal Shares Slide on Demand Concerns
briefs.body: Nucor dropped 6.32% and Alpha Metallurgical Resources fell 5.69% on Friday, dragging the Materials sector to a –1.05% close. The paired decline points to softening expectations for industrial metals demand, a theme likely to be tested by any macro data or manufacturing prints due later in the week.

briefs.headline: Iran Escalation Adds Layer of Complexity to Middle East Risk Calculus
briefs.body: Tehran warned against further escalation by the United States and its allies, closed a French cultural centre amid accusations of illegal activity, and carried out an execution linked to alleged Israeli intelligence operations — a cluster of moves that collectively raised the regional tension backdrop investors must weigh as the new trading week begins.
